more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Sodium thiosulphate is an inorganic sodium salt chemically distinct from sodium sulphite. FDA describes manufacturing routes involving sulphur and sulphite, or reactions and oxidation of sulphide materials. Its listed direct-food functions are formulation assistance and reduction, with applications in alcoholic beverages and table salt. JECFA also identifies preservative and antioxidant functions for this compound.
more_info.daily_intake: 0-0.7 mg/kg body weight (JECFA, 1998). The JECFA group limit is expressed as sulphur dioxide equivalents.
more_info.origin: Chemically manufactured. FDA describes production from sulphides and sulphur dioxide, from sulphur and sulphite, or by oxidation of metal sulphides or hydrosulphides.
more_info.uses: FDA lists formulation-aid and reducing-agent uses in alcoholic beverages and table salt. The stated maximum levels are 0.00005% and 0.1%, respectively, in the served foods.
